Strait of Hormuz Status: October 14, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
14 October 2026 .
Brent $ 106.06 -0.25 % · Transits 2 (2026-10-11) · AI-assisted
01 BBC reports a Singapore-flagged container ship sank in the Strait of Hormuz after being hit by a projectile, though the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore says no injuries were reported from two Singapore-registered vessels struck, per Yahoo News Singapore and The Straits Times.

02 Brent stood at $106.06, down 0.25% over 24 hours, as of 20:59 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 2 transits on October 11, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

03 gCaptain reports US forces destroyed an Iranian-affiliated dhow in the Gulf of Oman on October 6 after determining it was conducting surveillance and helping target American warships, per gCaptain.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains the site of intensifying attacks on merchant shipping. BBC reports that a Singapore-flagged container ship sank after being struck by a projectile in the strait, a claim gCaptain also carries; however, the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore says no injuries were reported from two Singapore-registered ships struck in the strait, per Yahoo News Singapore and The Straits Times, leaving the full picture of that incident contested. The Guardian and WSJ report that two ships sank near the strait as Iranian attacks intensified, and The Japan Times reports that Iran has been shifting tactics in its attacks on shipping. Per Iranian state media, a cargo ship sank after striking a mine in the strait; that claim originates with the IRGC and has not been carried by a major wire in this feed. gCaptain reports that US forces destroyed an Iranian-affiliated dhow in the Gulf of Oman on October 6, determining it was conducting surveillance and helping target American warships. IMF PortWatch recorded 2 transits on October 11, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent stood at $106.06, down 0.25% over 24 hours, as of 20:59 UTC. The feed indexed 110 headlines in the last 24 hours. Iran's closure posture and its seven-condition framework remain in force, with no resolution reported in this window. As of 21:22 UTC, 141 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, flat over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
